entry.title: Open-Source Out-of-Order RISC-V Vector Core with Speculative Matrix Register Renaming
entry.summary:
Long-vector and tile matrix instructions stall superscalar pipelines when register file ports saturate during mixed FP8/BF16 kernels. We present an open-source SystemVerilog RISC-V (`RV64GCV`) core taped out in $5\text{ nm}$ that decouples matrix accumulator renaming from scalar ROB entries, achieving $3.1\text{ TFLOPS/W}$.

Source: arXiv Hardware Architecture (cs.AR) · Tags: #computer-architecture #semiconductors #open-source

entry.title: Hardware-Enforced Capability Tagging Eliminates Use-After-Free in Kernel Network Rings
entry.summary:
High-speed `io_uring` and zero-copy DMA rings remain prime targets for page-level use-after-free exploitation in the Linux kernel. By binding descriptor rings to fine-grained CHERI/MTE memory capability tags verified at the IOMMU boundary, packet throughput stays within $1.8\%$ of baseline at $400\text{ Gb/s}$ while deterministically trapping temporal aliasing.

Source: LWN.net / Systems Architecture · Tags: #kernel-os #infosec #computer-architecture

entry.title: Cross-Cache Speculative Type Confusion in Modern Browser JIT Tier-Up Pipelines
entry.summary:
Optimizing JIT compilers elide bounds and map checks when profiling feedback indicates monomorphic object shapes. We demonstrate a speculative race condition during concurrent background compilation that leaks arbitrary WebAssembly linear memory across site isolation boundaries in under $90\text{ ms}$, along with a zero-overhead fence mitigation.

Source: Google Project Zero / InfoSec · Tags: #infosec #compilers #performance
